fatigue_fraction.source: Carbide fatigue / TRS: 0.33–0.42 fully reversed or 10⁶–10⁸ cycles (Schleinkofer 1996, Kursawe 2001, Brookes, Schedler via Preis 2004); 0.375 × 3.8 GPa = 1425 MPa adopted for C4 (Round 4); docs/research/carbide_and_edge_radius.md §2

edge_radius_mm.source: micro end mills 0.4–3.5 µm (Liang 2018; Jäckel 2024); no data vs diameter; not calibrated (C1 rarely binds above 1/32")

C2.basis: data/model_v2/chip_limits.json (band median of worst-flute h/D, eccentric runout at TIR 0.0002")
C2.source: confirmed on the hold-out rows against fitted alternatives (calibration_report.json c2)

aggressiveness.status: PROPOSAL for the user (design §3.6); the optimizer still uses the Round 1 placeholder map

C2_scale.form: piecewise linear in a between the points
C2_scale.source: the vendor rows' own spread of worst-flute h/D around each band median: p25/median and p75/median, median over bands (calibration_report.json)

C4_limit_mpa.source: cited fatigue fractions of TRS 3.8 GPa: 0.33 (Schleinkofer 1996, R = −1, 10⁷, via Preis 2004), 0.375 (Round 4 basis), 0.42 (Kursawe 2001, 10⁶ cycles ≈ a tool's life, via Preis 2004). The current ×1.3 at a = 1 is 0.49·TRS, above any cited fully reversed level

life_ratio.source: with n = 0.25 this moves speed ×0.84…×1.19, about the inter-quartile spread of vendor speed levels (vendor_effect_log in calibration_report.json)

C5_margin.source: placeholder; the spindle is a hard limit

C3.source: C3 is the user's process requirement (50 % of the stock to leave)
